task_instance: Generate a legal-response for a sample Data Subject Access Request (GDPR) from a customer: created a sample inbound inquiry, ran the skill's escalation-trigger check (no trigger detected), created a DSR acknowledgment template (since no team templates were configured, per Step 2/Step 6 of the skill), and generated the customized final response with escalation-check notes and follow-up actions.
evidence: Work performed entirely with text files in the work directory (no shell, no code execution, no binaries needed, matching the skill's actual deliverable of a markdown/text response draft). Files produced: inquiry.md (sample input DSR from 'Maria Gonzalez', GDPR access request, received 2026-09-25), dsr-acknowledgment-template.md (a template built per the skill's 'Template Creation Guide' since no pre-existing templates were found in the work directory), and generated-response.md (the final populated response, in the skill's specified 'Output Format' with To/Subject/body/Escalation Check/Follow-Up Actions sections). Verified the deliverable by re-reading the escalation trigger lists in SKILL.md (lines 66-73, Data Subject Request Escalation Triggers) and confirming each of the 7 listed conditions against the sample facts in inquiry.md, none of which apply, so the escalation check documented in generated-response.md correctly concludes no escalation and a templated draft is appropriate. All variables ({{requester_name}}, {{request_id}}, {{response_deadline}}, etc.) in the template were correctly substituted with concrete values (Maria Gonzalez, DSR-2026-0142, 2026-10-25) in the final response, and the GDPR one-month deadline calculation (2026-09-25 + 1 month = 2026-10-25) was checked by hand. The task needed no code execution, no binary output, and no external/paid/credentialed services -- it is fully achievable within the office-assistant's read/write/edit-text-files capability.
